source TEXT
package TEXT
version TEXT
who_json TEXT
criteria_json TEXT
PRIMARY KEY(source, package, version, who_json)
One row per full audit per source. The key includes
the auditor, because covers() filters on who signed it.
Delta audits are dropped rather than stored: resolving
a delta chain back to a full audit is out of scope.

div.div:
artifact_cache (metadata only; bytes live on disk)
sha256 PRIMARY KEY -- content-addressed, not per package
ecosystem, package, version, filename, bytes, last_access
index_cache (PyPI simple index pages)
package PRIMARY KEY, body, fetched_at
A cache hit is only as good as the hash that admitted it.
A cache read error is never fatal: it falls through to a
fresh download. Cache failure cannot change a verdict.

div.div: The fingerprint column is the invalidation mechanism. Every verdict records the policy fingerprint it was decided under, so changing the CVE line, the plugins, the AI model, the prompt or collector version, or an ecosystem's release-age threshold re-keys every row and forces a rescan. Changing the allowlist deliberately does NOT change the fingerprint: it narrows trust rather than changing what is checked.
